signature: SUBROUTINE DLARRD( RANGE, ORDER, N, VL, VU, IL, IU, GERS,

params.name: range
params.reference:
-   `= 'A'`: ("All")   all eigenvalues will be found.
-   `= 'V'`: ("Value") all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`, `VU`\] will be found.
-   `= 'I'`: ("Index") the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues (of the entire matrix) will be found.

params.name: order
params.reference:
-   `= 'B'`: ("By Block") the eigenvalues will be grouped by split-off block (see `IBLOCK`, `ISPLIT`) and ordered from smallest to largest within the block.
-   `= 'E'`: ("Entire matrix") the eigenvalues for the entire matrix will be ordered from smallest to largest.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the tridiagonal matrix T. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: vl
params.reference: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. Eigenvalues less than or equal to `VL`, or greater than `VU`, will not be returned. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.

params.name: vu
params.reference: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. Eigenvalues less than or equal to `VL`, or greater than `VU`, will not be returned. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.

params.name: il
params.reference: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.

params.name: iu
params.reference: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.

params.name: GERS
params.reference: The N Gerschgorin intervals (the i-th Gerschgorin interval is (`GERS(2*i-1)`, `GERS(2*i)`).

params.name: reltol
params.reference: The minimum relative width of an interval. When an interval is narrower than `RELTOL` times the larger (in magnitude) endpoint, then it is considered to be sufficiently small, i.e., converged. Note: this should always be at least radix\*machine $\epsilon$.

params.name: d
params.reference: The n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.

params.name: e
params.reference: The (n-1) off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.

params.name: E2
params.reference: The (n-1) squared off-diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.

params.name: pivmin
params.reference: The minimum pivot allowed in the Sturm sequence for T.

params.name: nsplit
params.reference: The number of diagonal blocks in the matrix T. $1 \le \mathrm{NSPLIT} \le N$.

params.name: ISPLIT
params.reference: The splitting points, at which T breaks up into submatrices. The first submatrix consists of rows/columns 1 to `ISPLIT(1)`, the second of rows/columns `ISPLIT(1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(2)`, etc., and the `NSPLIT`-th consists of rows/columns `ISPLIT(NSPLIT-1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(NSPLIT)=N`. (Only the first `NSPLIT` elements will actually be used, but since the user cannot know a priori what value `NSPLIT` will have, N words must be reserved for `ISPLIT`.)

params.name: m
params.reference: The actual number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. (See also the description of `INFO=2`,3.)

params.name: w
params.reference: On exit, the first M elements of W will contain the eigenvalue approximations. DLARRD computes an interval I\_j = (a\_j, b\_j\] that includes eigenvalue j. The eigenvalue approximation is given as the interval midpoint `W(j)`= ( a\_j + b\_j)/2. The corresponding error is bounded by `WERR(j)` = abs( a\_j - b\_j)/2

params.name: WERR
params.reference: The error bound on the corresponding eigenvalue approximation in W.

params.name: wu
params.reference:
The interval (`WL`, `WU`\] contains all the wanted eigenvalues. If `RANGE='V'`, then `WL=VL` and `WU=VU`. If `RANGE='A'`, then `WL` and `WU` are the global Gerschgorin bounds

on the spectrum.

If `RANGE='I'`, then `WL` and `WU` are computed by DLAEBZ from the

index range specified.

params.name: IBLOCK
params.reference: At each row/column j where `E(j)` is zero or small, the matrix T is considered to split into a block diagonal matrix. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `IBLOCK(i)` specifies to which block (from 1 to the number of blocks) the eigenvalue `W(i)` belongs. (DLARRD may use the remaining N-M elements as workspace.)

params.name: INDEXW
params.reference: The indices of the eigenvalues within each block (submatrix); for example, `INDEXW(i)= j` and `IBLOCK(i)=k` imply that the i-th eigenvalue `W(i)` is the j-th eigenvalue in block k.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: some or all of the eigenvalues failed to converge or were not computed: =1 or 3: Bisection failed to converge for some eigenvalues; these eigenvalues are flagged by a negative block number.  The effect is that the eigenvalues may not be as accurate as the absolute and relative tolerances.  This is generally caused by unexpectedly inaccurate arithmetic. =2 or 3: `RANGE='I'` only: Not all of the eigenvalues `IL`:`IU` were found. Effect: $M < \mathrm{IU}+1-\mathrm{IL}$ Cause:  non-monotonic arithmetic, causing the Sturm sequence to be non-monotonic. Cure:   recalculate, using `RANGE='A'`, and pick out eigenvalues `IL`:`IU`.  In some cases, increasing the PARAMETER "FUDGE" may make things work.
-   `= 4`: `RANGE='I'`, and the Gershgorin interval initially used was too small.  No eigenvalues were computed. Probable cause: your machine has sloppy floating-point arithmetic. Cure: Increase the PARAMETER "FUDGE", recompile, and try again.
